#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: A shipping form asks for country, region and city in one field: a .cascader with three levels submits place=us, place=ca and place=sf; a single country choice stays a select.

#### Contract

Pick a path through nested options shown in columns, where each choice opens the next column, and submit the whole path.

Write a `.field.cascader` holding a text `<input>` with a `name`, its `<label for>`, and a `ul.cascader-options` of nested lists. Each `<li>` holds a `data-value`, and its label is its own text outside any nested list. An `<li>` with a nested list of options is a branch; any other is a leaf. `AutoInit()` starts every `.cascader`. The lists stay in the page, hidden, and the script builds the columns from them; leave roles off them.

The input becomes read-only, with `role="combobox"` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. A click, or Enter, Space, ArrowDown or Alt+ArrowDown, opens a popover below the field with `role="dialog"`. Each column is a listbox named by the field's label or by the option that opened it, and the options on the open path are `aria-selected="true"`. A branch ends in a chevron.

#### Syntax

```html
<div class="field cascader">
  <input id="place" name="place" type="text" required>
  <label for="place">Place</label>
  <ul class="cascader-options">
    <li data-value="us">United States
      <ul>
        <li data-value="ca">California
          <ul>
            <li data-value="sf">San Francisco</li>
            <li data-value="la">Los Angeles</li>
          </ul>
        </li>
        <li data-value="wa">Washington</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li data-value="cn">Canada</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `i18n` | Object | `{ required: 'Choose an option.' }` | `required` is the validity message while a required field has no path. Markup sets it with `data-cascader-options='{"i18n":{"required":"Elige un lugar."}}'` on the `.cascader`. |

#### Methods

- `.open()`: Opens the popover at the committed path, with focus on its leaf or on the first option. A disabled field does not open.
- `.close()`: Closes the popover and keeps the committed path.
- `.destroy()`: Closes and removes the popover, unwraps the input, and gives back its name, `required` and attributes. The input keeps its text.

#### Also documented

The Cascader section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Properties.

#### Rules

- `cascader-lists-take-no-roles`: Leave roles off .cascader-options and its items. The lists are the source the script reads; it builds the listbox columns, with their roles and states, itself.
- `cascader-option-has-value`: Give every option in .cascader-options a data-value. The form submits one value per level of the chosen path, and an option without one submits an empty string.
- `cascader-needs-a-text-field`: A .cascader shows the chosen path in an <input> of type text, which the script makes read-only. Other input types reject the path's labels.
- `cascader-input-is-named`: Name the cascader's input with a <label for> in the field, or aria-label. The popover and its first column take their name from the same label.
